query:
title: Resolve conflicting legacy and management C# emitter diagnostics

question: Our ARM TypeSpec project already uses @azure-typespec/http-client-csharp-mgmt. After rebasing, generation reports Rule FlavorAzure failed and asks for options.@azure-tools/typespec-csharp.flavor: azure. I added that legacy emitter block, but now SdkTspConfigValidation says the project must not use it. How should I resolve these conflicting errors?
ground_truth: For this migrated management-plane project, keep the supported @azure-typespec/http-client-csharp-mgmt configuration and remove the deprecated @azure-tools/typespec-csharp block rather than retaining both to satisfy conflicting diagnostics. Preserve the package namespace and output path under the supported emitter. Check the configuration and supported options against the pinned management emitter, rerun config validation and generation, and inspect the result. If the original diagnostic persists, investigate the actual pinned tooling/configuration instead of assuming legacy config is required. Do not substitute the data-plane emitter for this ARM SDK.

query:
title: Keep spec fixes while targeting an earlier management API version

question: I validated client.tsp naming fixes locally with LocalSpecRepo, but the same specs checkout also contains 2026-08-01-preview, which C# generation now selects. Our ARM SDK release must still target 2026-07-01. How can I keep the newer spec fixes without generating the preview API, and what should I verify before updating the SDK PR?
ground_truth: Select the API version independently of the spec revision: set api-version: 2026-07-01 under @azure-typespec/http-client-csharp-mgmt in the spec project's tspconfig.yaml while generating from the revision or local project containing the client.tsp fixes. Regenerate and inspect both the selected API version and corrected generated names. Ensure the intended spec/configuration changes are recorded for reproducible SDK generation, updating tsp-location.yaml to the intended merged spec commit when appropriate. Do not roll back the needed fixes solely to avoid the preview or edit generated API-version constants as the lasting fix.

query:
title: Update samples and regenerate after management spec review fixes

question: Our new management API replaces a model, so the hand-maintained .NET samples no longer compile. I also have a separate spec change fixing generated class names after review, but those names are not reflected in the SDK PR yet. Can I edit the samples directly, and how should I bring the naming fixes into the SDK? Is there a Copilot workflow that can help with these review fixes?
ground_truth: Update the hand-maintained samples to the intended SDK API; SDK generation does not rewrite those samples. Separately regenerate the SDK using the spec changes containing the naming fixes instead of manually patching generated C#. Inspect the generated API and build the samples/library to verify both changes. Record the intended spec revision in tsp-location.yaml once the spec fixes merge so subsequent generation reproduces the result. For Copilot assistance, recommend the management-specific mgmt-review-comment-resolution skill in azure-sdk-for-net and direct the author to its instructions; the author must run and review the workflow, not assume the bot has applied fixes or obtained approval.

query:
title: Select the C# emitter for Azure management and data-plane SDKs

question: I'm setting up TypeSpec generation for two Azure .NET SDKs: an ARM management SDK and an Azure data-plane SDK. Which C# emitter should each project use, and where do I configure it?
ground_truth: Use @azure-typespec/http-client-csharp-mgmt for the ARM management SDK and @azure-typespec/http-client-csharp for the Azure data-plane SDK. Select the appropriate emitter in the TypeSpec project's tspconfig.yaml emit list and put its options under the matching options key. These emitters serve different SDK types; do not substitute one for the other or recommend the deprecated @azure-tools/typespec-csharp emitter.

query:
title: Generate a .NET SDK from a local TypeSpec project

question: I'm working in azure-sdk-for-net and want to generate a data-plane SDK from uncommitted changes in my local azure-rest-api-specs checkout. What command should I run, and should LocalSpecRepo point to the repository root, main.tsp, or a directory inside the checkout?
ground_truth: From the SDK project's src directory, run dotnet build /t:GenerateCode /p:LocalSpecRepo="<local TypeSpec project directory>". LocalSpecRepo must identify the directory containing tspconfig.yaml and main.tsp, corresponding to the directory in tsp-location.yaml, not the repository root or the main.tsp file itself. This uses the local spec project instead of the normal repo/commit sync configured in tsp-location.yaml.

query:
title: Configure the API version for management C# generation

question: Our TypeSpec service has several API versions. How do I configure the management C# emitter to generate only 2026-07-01, and which version does it generate if I don't set that option?
ground_truth: Set api-version: 2026-07-01 under options.@azure-typespec/http-client-csharp-mgmt in the project's tspconfig.yaml. The management emitter defaults to the latest version when this option is omitted. Regenerate after changing the configuration; do not edit generated C# API-version constants to select the generation target.

query:
title: Address management SDK breaking changes instead of masking diagnostics

question: I added an eng/apicompatbaselines XML file in my management .NET SDK PR to suppress compatibility errors. After merging main and regenerating, the PR is still flagged for suppressed breaking changes. Is deleting that new file enough, or how should I address the underlying breaks? Can Copilot help find supported mitigations?
ground_truth: Merging main and regenerating do not themselves mitigate released API breaks or remove the added suppression. Inspect the actual ApiCompat diagnostics against the previous released contract, choose supported spec/SDK customizations that preserve required APIs, and regenerate and rerun compatibility checks. Remove the newly introduced suppression as the corresponding breaks are addressed; do not merely delete it and declare success or delete unrelated approved baselines. Recommend the management-specific mitigate-breaking-changes skill in azure-sdk-for-net for Copilot assistance, with the author reviewing the changes and results. Do not invent an exact mitigation without diagnostics or substitute blanket suppression for required review of an intentional break.

query:
title: Investigate wire field casing when the public .NET API is unchanged

question: A TypeSpec change alters a JSON field from name to Name. We keep the same .NET member name with clientName, CI passes, and APIView has no diff. Does that mean deserialization cannot change? What should I inspect or test before treating this as compatible?
ground_truth: The unchanged public member explains why APIView can have no diff even though the JSON wire contract changes. APIView and ApiCompat cover public API compatibility, not proof of runtime or wire compatibility. Regenerate from the changed spec, inspect the actual serialization/deserialization changes, and test representative payloads using the relevant field casing against the intended service contract. Assess behavior for existing consumers rather than declaring compatibility from green CI or an empty APIView alone; do not assume a particular serializer's case-handling behavior without checking the generated implementation.

query:
title: Generated C# method remains after adding CodeGenSuppress

question: Hi, I added a custom replacement for a generated C# SDK method and used CodeGenSuppress to suppress the original. The generated method is still there, though, and the build fails with CS0111 because both methods have the same signature. What should I check to get the suppression applied without editing the generated files?
ground_truth: CodeGenSuppress is consumed during SDK code generation; adding the attribute alone does not remove an existing generated method. Check whether generation ran after the customization was added and rerun it with that customization included. Do not assume generation was skipped without checking. If the generated method remains, verify that the suppression targets the exact method name and ordered parameter types. Inspect the regenerated diff and rebuild to confirm the intended custom replacement remains without a duplicate generated method. Do not delete or patch generated files as the lasting fix, or conclude that a generator defect is the cause from this symptom alone.

query:
title: Keep C# customizations outside generated files

question: I need to add C#-only behavior to a generated SDK model, but my edits under src/Generated disappear when I regenerate. Where should I put the customization so that it survives generation?
ground_truth: Do not rely on manual edits to generated files. First consider a supported TypeSpec/client.tsp customization when it can express the change. For C# behavior that cannot be expressed there, use a handwritten partial class outside the generated directory, with the matching model namespace and type name. Regenerate and build to verify that the generated and handwritten parts work together and the customization is preserved.
